final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype score (0.992) at a conserved catalytic-loop glycine; near-zero MSA and PLM plausibility indicate the substitution is highly disruptive, supporting loss of catalytic function.
Very high phenotype score (0.991) at the active-site lysine involved in PLP binding; negligible homolog and PLM tolerance consistent with severe functional loss.
Strong phenotype score (0.971) at a second catalytic-region glycine; slight evolutionary tolerance lowers certainty relative to G307D but remains a strong LOF candidate.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidates are stable across phenotype, MSA, and PLM evidence; further tool calls are unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Cys52 is the heme-ligating cysteine; substitution with bulky Tyr disrupts heme coordination, a known LOF mechanism in CBS deficiency.
C52 is the heme axial ligand; disrupting it strongly impairs CBS function. Retain pending tool evidence.
Phenotype 0.878 is pathogenic-class and PLP-binding Cys52 disruption is mechanistically strong for LOF, but it trails the top three on the phenotype dimension.

Strong phenotype (0.878) and no homolog tolerance, but Zn-binding Cys loss may destabilize folding rather than cleanly abolish catalysis. Lower confidence and rank below the catalytic glycine/lysine variants.
His65 coordinates the heme iron on the distal side; replacing it abolishes heme binding and severely impairs catalysis.
H65 is the second heme axial ligand; mutating it should directly abolish heme binding and enzyme activity, so I raise it above several weaker candidates.
Phenotype 0.357 is ambiguous, clearly the weakest on the dimension closest to the reward; removed from the pool.

rejection.reason: Phenotype 0.357 is ambiguous, clearly the weakest on the dimension closest to the reward; removed from the pool.

history.rationale: Lys119 lies in the PLP-binding region; mutating the conserved catalytic lysine to a neutral residue blocks the internal aldimine and PLP chemistry.
K119 is the PLP internal aldimine lysine in the catalytic domain; substitution to a non-basic residue should abolish PLP attachment and catalysis.
Phenotype 0.991 (top-tier) with near-zero MSA mutant frequency and lowest PLM plausibility; Lys119 is a conserved catalytic-domain residue whose substitution to Asn removes a positive charge.
Very high phenotype score (0.991) at the active-site lysine that binds PLP; conservation and plausibility near zero consistent with severe functional impact. Retain as rank 2.
Arg121 is a conserved active-site-region residue; a charge-reversal-to-bulk substitution frequently appears among pathogenic CBS missense alleles.
Neighboring the PLP lysine but less directly catalytic; keep in pool pending phenotype/functional-annotation evidence.
Phenotype 0.895 and zero evolutionary tolerance support LOF, but mechanistic rationale is weaker than the catalytic-site candidates.
Good phenotype score (0.895) but slightly lower confidence than C52Y due to less direct catalytic role; kept as backup.
T191M is a recurrent pathogenic CBS missense variant that destabilizes the catalytic core and reduces activity.
Known pathogenic hotspot in CBS; plausibly destabilizes the active-site PLP environment, but mechanistically less direct than ligand mutations.
Phenotype 0.716 is below the leaders; retained as backup only.
Moderate phenotype (0.716) and, unlike the leaders, some evolutionary tolerance (0.036 relative to pool) and conservative chemistry make it a weaker LOF bet. Drop to keep the pool focused.

rejection.reason: Moderate phenotype (0.716) and, unlike the leaders, some evolutionary tolerance (0.036 relative to pool) and conservative chemistry make it a weaker LOF bet. Drop to keep the pool focused.

history.rationale: Glu239 is a conserved catalytic-domain acidic residue; the E239K charge reversal disrupts active-site electrostatics.
Moderate prior for destabilizing the catalytic core; rank below active-site ligand mutations.
Phenotype 0.828 but position is less conserved (entropy 2.6, some K tolerance); backup only.
Weakest mechanistic link to the active site and only mid-range phenotype score (0.828). Drop from active pool.

rejection.reason: Weakest mechanistic link to the active site and only mid-range phenotype score (0.828). Drop from active pool.

history.rationale: Gly305 sits in the conserved GIGYDFI active-site motif; introducing Asp breaks the tight PLP-site backbone geometry.
Glycine in PLP-domain region; Asp may disrupt local backbone but effect on activity uncertain.
Phenotype 0.971 strongly supports LOF; some evolutionary tolerance of D at 305 (0.11) slightly tempers confidence, but ESM-1v plausibility is at the floor.
Strong phenotype score (0.971) at a second catalytic-region glycine; modest evolutionary tolerance (0.114) slightly weakens certainty versus G307D. Retain as rank 3.
Gly307 is in the same conserved active-site motif as Gly305; an Asp here distorts the PLP/substrate pocket.
Same region as G305D; plausible structural disruption but weaker mechanistic link than ligand residues.

Highest phenotype (LOF proxy) score 0.992 with zero evolutionary tolerance and lowest ESM-1v plausibility, all consistent with strong loss of function in the catalytic domain. Gly->Asp at a strictly conserved glycine is mechanistically disruptive.
Highest phenotype score (0.992) at a conserved catalytic-loop glycine; PLM and MSA scores near zero confirm the variant is highly disruptive, which supports LOF. Retain as rank 1.
A114V is a documented pathogenic CBS variant in the heme/PLP interdomain region that lowers enzyme activity.
Conservative substitution with weak mechanistic rationale for abolishing activity; drop to make room for stronger catalytic-site candidates.

rejection.reason: Conservative substitution with weak mechanistic rationale for abolishing activity; drop to make room for stronger catalytic-site candidates.

history.rationale: Pro145 in the conserved TIIEPT motif constrains the active-site loop; Leu substitution likely perturbs PLP positioning.
No direct catalytic or ligand role documented; low expected LOF yield, remove from pool.

rejection.reason: No direct catalytic or ligand role documented; low expected LOF yield, remove from pool.
